title: HEP Proxy Validation (EP-0)
description: Heart-Evoked Potential (HEP) Proxy Validation Sub-Protocol (EP-0). Validates HEP amplitude as an operational proxy for interoceptive precision weighting (Pi_i), establishing the foundational empirical grounding for downstream protocols EP-1, EP-8, and EP-11.

sub_predictions.claim: HEP amplitude correlates with interoceptive accuracy (heartbeat detection task performance)
sub_predictions.confirming_evidence: HEP amplitude (250-400 ms post-R-wave) is significantly larger in high-IA vs. low-IA participants.
sub_predictions.falsifying_evidence: No significant HEP difference between high- and low-IA groups (p > 0.05, corrected).

sub_predictions.claim: Source-localised HEP generators implicate anterior insula and/or vmPFC
sub_predictions.confirming_evidence: Dipole fitting or beamformer source localisation places dominant HEP generator in anterior insula or vmPFC ROI.
sub_predictions.falsifying_evidence: HEP is exclusively generated by primary somatosensory or auditory cortex, with no anterior insula component.

validation_notes: EP-0 stub — no runtime implementation yet. Partial falsification coverage exists in FP_09_NeuralSignaturesP3bHEP.py. A full implementation requires ECG+EEG recordings with heartbeat detection task and source localisation pipeline.

inclusion_criteria: Adequate ECG signal quality (R-peak detection accuracy > 95%)
exclusion_criteria: Cardiac arrhythmia or irregular heartbeat patterns
Excessive EEG artifact contaminating HEP window (250-400 ms post-R-wave)
Failure to complete heartbeat detection task (accuracy < chance + 10%)
Neurological or psychiatric diagnosis affecting interoceptive processing

apparatus.execution_environment: APGI desktop application and local project runtime

target.type: Cardiac epoch — 500 ms window locked to ECG R-peak

trial_structure.response: Heartbeat detection rating (4AFC: definitely yes, probably yes, probably no, definitely no) or continuous interoceptive accuracy score
trial_structure.session_structure: Resting HEP block (200 epochs) followed by heartbeat detection task (80 trials), counterbalanced

blocks.notes: 200 resting HEP epochs + 80 heartbeat detection trials. Block structure mirrors Garfinkel et al. (2014) heartbeat discrimination paradigm.

dependent_variables: HEP amplitude at 250-400 ms post-R-wave (frontocentral ROI, Fz/FCz/Cz)
Interoceptive accuracy score (heartbeat detection d-prime or proportion correct)
Source-localised HEP generator location (anterior insula / vmPFC ROI hit)
primary_hypothesis: HEP amplitude (250-400 ms post-R-wave) will be significantly larger in participants with high interoceptive accuracy, and source-localised HEP generators will implicate anterior insula or vmPFC, validating HEP as a proxy for APGI precision weight Pi_i.
primary_analysis: Two-group comparison (high-IA vs. low-IA median split) of HEP amplitude at frontocentral electrodes; Pearson/Spearman correlation between HEP amplitude and continuous IA score; source localisation via LORETA or beamformer.

power_analysis.based_on: Garfinkel et al. 2014 HEP-IA effect size estimate (d ≈ 0.55)

ethics.data_sharing: Anonymised EEG/ECG epochs available upon reasonable request following data sharing agreement.

submission_blocking_issues: No runtime Python implementation yet — VP_00_HEPProxyValidation.py is a documented stub only.
Heartbeat detection task paradigm code not integrated.
caveats: HEP is a group-level proxy for Pi_i — individual-trial estimates require single-trial HEP decomposition (ICA or regression-based).
FP_09_NeuralSignaturesP3bHEP.py provides partial falsification coverage from the falsification side only.
EP-0 is a sub-protocol feeding into EP-1 (EEG Interoceptive Gating), EP-8 (Psychophysical Threshold), and EP-11 (Active Inference).
